newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Deals in the making.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Deals in the making.

text.p: Asian debt markets eased through another slow day on Tuesday.
Bankers said Thai Danu Bank's debt traded in the secondary market was unaffected by news that the bank would take over, rather than merge, with troubled Finance One Plc.
The news was not entirely unexpected given earlier rumours that the merger idea would be scotched in favour of a takeover, the bankers said.
Thai bank paper is very illiquid and most issues have not traded much since widening out earlier this year as the problems in Thailand's financial sector became apparent.
The joining of banks and ailing finance companies is designed to help shore up the sector.
Thailand's central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond today announced that the government plans to issue another 20 billion baht in zero coupon bonds next week.
Proceeds of the zero coupon bonds will be used to bail out the troubled property and finance sectors.
The government's first issue of zero coupon bonds was oversubscribed.
Asian debt markets didn't offer much in the way of new issues on Tuesday, but news of a few new mandates emerged.
Mosel Vitelic plans to issue a US$100 million floating rate note issue via a special purpose vehicle called Vision 2000 Ventures Cayman Island, bankers said.
The deal will be fully guaranteed by Mosel Vitelic.
The facility has a final maturity of five years with put and call options in year three. It will pay a margin of 47.5 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate.
Citicorp International, Credit Lyonnais and Taiwan Cooperative Bank are the mandated arrangers, bankers noted.

Steel Authority of India reportedly has mandated Merrill Lynch and Lehman Brothers to arrange a 10-year fixed rate bond issue. The issue is expected to pay a margin of between 125 and 150 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
India's Power Finance Corp is expected to bring a 10-year deal to market via ING Barings, but some bankers speculated that the issue will be privately placed.
In the loan markets, Hong Kong ceramics maker and distributor Interform Ceramics Technologies Ltd has launched a US$20 million term loan facility via its special purpose company.
The facility has a maturity of three years and pays a margin of 175 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate.
Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan and Bali International Finance are arrangers for the deal.
Hong Kong's Fountain Set has increased its loan facility to HK$450 million from HK$250 million.
Foshan Development Co Ltd's loan facility has been increased to US$23 million from US$20 million due to oversubscription, arrangers KIMB Finance and Standard Chartered Bank said.
The borrower, Foshan Development Co, is a Hong Kong-incorporated window company wholly owned by the Foshan Municipal People's Government.
